data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2018 were GBP 107.368m. The report shows mixed prior-year reserve development: detailed LOB analysis records large adverse movements on prior-period provisions (notably Third party liability), while other years show releases. The syndicate attributes a material part of prior-year deterioration on the 2016 year to 2017 US catastrophe activity (Hurricanes Irma and Harvey ~GBP 6m) and notes 2018 catastrophe experience (Florence, Michael, California wildfires) remained within reinsurance retention. No single consolidated gross prior-year movement figure is explicitly provided in the accounts.
raw_causal_phrases: The significant movements in gross claims incurred in respect of claims provisions created at the end of the previous period are analysed as follows:
The 2016 year of account has been impacted by the 2017 US Cat activity (most significantly Hurricanes Irma and Harvey), making up cGBP 6m of the loss.
Loss experience has been impacted by the US Cat events Hurricanes Florence and Michael and California Wildfires, although estimates for each remain within the syndicate's reinsurance retention.
the volatility in Euro exchange rates and from some investment losses
data.data_quality_notes: No single explicit gross total for prior-year development (all > 1 year) was found. The note 'significant movements in gross claims incurred in respect of claims provisions created at the end of the previous period' gives LOB-level gross movements (used above). The reconciliation 'change in provision for claims' on the technical provisions includes current-year movements and so was not used as the prior-year movement source per extraction rules. A gross claims development triangle is present and included in _claims_triangle, but parsing alignment is imperfect; amounts are presented in the accounts in thousands. There is also an RITC disclosed in underwriting year accounts which can distort comparisons; caution is advised if attempting to sum a single PYD total from the triangle.
